entry.title: Login with Google (oAuth) - Finding Client ID & Secret in Google Cloud Console (2026)
entry.summary: Finding the oAuth Client ID/Secret in a massive console can feel like a needle-in-a-haystack situation! While Search is a powerful tool, it’s actually one of three main ways to locate your OAuth details. As of 2026, here are the most effective methods to find your Client ID and Secret: The search bar at the top of the Google Cloud Console is highly optimized for "lost" users. Keywords to use: Type Credentials, OAuth, or Clients. The Result: Usually, the first result under "Products & Pages" will be APIs & Services > Credentials or the newer Google Auth Platform > Clients. Clicking this will take you directly to the list of all your IDs. Sometimes the UI hides the Secret behind a "Copy" icon or inside an "Edit" sub-menu to prevent "shoulder surfing" (people looking at your screen). If you see your Client ID in a list but can't find the Secret, look for the Download JSON icon (usually a small tray with an arrow) on the far right of the row. Open that file in any text editor. It will explicitly list: "client_id": "your-id-here" "client_secret": "your-secret-here" If you prefer navigating the sidebar, Google has consolidated identity tools. Check these two paths: Primary Path: Navigation Menu (☰) > APIs & Services > Credentials. Newer Consolidated Path: Navigation Menu (☰) > Google Auth Platform > Clients. (Google is increasingly moving OAuth-specific tasks here to keep them separate from backend API keys). The "Secret-less" Client: If you are looking for a secret for an Android, iOS, or Chrome client ID, you won't find one. Google doesn't issue secrets for these platforms because they are considered "public clients" where a secret cannot be safely hidden in the code. The "Eye" Icon: On the Credential details page, look for a small eye icon next to a masked field (••••••••). Clicking this will reveal the secret without you having to download a file.

entry.title: Nous Research's NousCoder-14B is an open-source coding model landing right in the Claude Code moment
entry.summary: Nous Research, the open-source artificial intelligence startup backed by crypto venture firm Paradigm, released a new competitive programming model on Monday that it says matches or exceeds several larger proprietary systems — trained in just four days using 48 of Nvidia's latest B200 graphics processors. The model, called NousCoder-14B, is another entry in a crowded field of AI coding assistants, but arrives at a particularly charged moment: Claude Code, the agentic programming tool from rival Anthropic, has dominated social media discussion since New Year's Day, with developers posting breathless testimonials about its capabilities.
